name: Salicylic acid peel
lead: A salicylic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel using salicylic acid, a beta-hydroxy acid (BHA), commonly at 20 to 30% in clinical studies and used mainly for acne and pigmentation [1][2]. Wikipedia describes salicylic acid as antibacterial and anti-inflammatory and increasingly preferred over AHAs because it is oil-soluble, though the oil-solubility claim is flagged there as needing a citation [7].
Published evidence consists mostly of small comparative studies and registered trials. A 2014 study compared 50% pyruvic and 30% salicylic peels on sebum secretion in 20 people with acne [1].

paras: The 2014 comparison of 50% pyruvic acid and 30% salicylic acid peels in 20 men and women aged 13 to 30 with acne measured facial sebum secretion [1].

Registered trials have compared 30% salicylic acid with 25% trichloroacetic acid in mild to moderate acne (60 participants, completed) [2], combined it with 4% hydroquinone for melasma in Hispanic women [3], compared it with glycolic acid for melasma [4] and for post-acne scars [5], and compared peel types in acne [6]. Results of these registrations are not summarized in the available records.

Wikipedia notes that complications rise with peel depth and can include prolonged redness, pigment changes, milia and skin thinning, and that light peels commonly cause stinging, redness, irritation and dryness. [7]

card.summary: The oil-soluble BHA peel most often studied for acne, supported by small comparative studies.
card.note: Superficial peels commonly cause stinging, redness and dryness.

quick.overview:
A salicylic acid peel uses a beta-hydroxy acid at roughly 20 to 30% to exfoliate the skin, mainly for acne and some pigmentation.

Evidence is mostly small studies and trial registrations comparing it with other peels.
quick.mechanism: Wikipedia describes salicylic acid as antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and oil-soluble, which is why it is associated with acne-prone skin.
quick.risks: Light peels commonly cause stinging, redness, irritation and dryness; deeper peels carry higher complication risks such as pigment change.
